items.title: 67750_Sippie Wallace oral history interview
items.q: Bessie would come to your house and she'd buy everything you had to drink

ctx.x: What do you mean, Bessie was a different kind of mean than Vicki?

She was ________. Bessie would come to your house and she'd buy everything you had to drink (unintelligible). She would ask you how much drinks you got, maybe you say, "I got a quart, bottle quart of whiskey." "Just set the damn quart up." She'd say, "Get the damn quart

up on the table." And then maybe you got three or four people and say, "Now, call so and so and so and so in here," say, "Now, (unintelligible)." (Unintelligible) and I told Buddy, Sue, I said, "I can't stand that woman." I said, "I can't stand that woman." And I didn't like her because she cussed too much. She really wasn't my type. I don't like no cussing woman. (Inaudible). People don't want you cussing. Just like (unintelligible) frown. People don't want you to frown (unintelligible) smiles.
